title: Exercise After Breast Augmentation: Week-by-Week Plan
meta_description: Walk from day one, add harder cardio at about 2 weeks. After that sources split: a month to 6 weeks for strenuous exercise. Week by week, source by source.
excerpt: Exercise comes back in stages, and the sources do not all agree. Here is a week-by-week plan that sets them side by side, from walking on day one to the push-up question, with a table for weeks 4 and 5 and what the one randomized trial found.
quick_answer:
When can you work out after breast augmentation?

Walk from the first day. One article on the ASPS website adds harder cardio at about 2 weeks and most exercise at about a month, but MedlinePlus says no strenuous exercise for 3 to 6 weeks and another article says at least six weeks. Cleveland Clinic says no heavy lifting for at least 4 weeks. Your surgeon decides.

Exercise After Breast Augmentation: What the Sources Say
From day 1: Light walking
After about 2 weeks: Harder cardio, such as treadmill or uphill walking (an article on the ASPS website)
First month: No sports that raise your pulse (Sientra labeling)
For 3 to 4 weeks: No strenuous activity (University of Utah Health)
About a month: Most exercise, except heavy lifting (the same ASPS website article)
For 3 to 6 weeks: No strenuous exercise or heavy lifting (MedlinePlus)
For at least 6 weeks: No strenuous activity or upper body movements (another ASPS website article)
Sources differ. Your surgeon sets your dates.

sources.publisher: ASPS website, blog by Catherine Huang-Begovic, MD
sources.title: Exercise after breast augmentation
quotes: Patients should start light walking immediately after surgery
This is good for the circulation and helps prevent blood clots.
After two weeks, patients can start more intense cardio such as walking on a treadmill or walking uphill.
At a month most patients can resume most exercise except heavy lifting.
At six weeks, patients are generally completely healed and can resume all exercises.
After breast augmentation, especially with implants under the muscle, I recommend patients try to avoid strenuous chest exercise such as push ups.
Since the implants sit under the muscle, contraction places downward and outward pressure on them which, over time can result in the implants dropping or becoming displaced over time.
if they do something that causes swelling or discomfort, stop doing it and give it a little more time.
Definitely use a good supportive bra when exercising

sources.publisher: ASPS website, article by Ariel Frankeny, freelance writer
sources.title: Back to active: Returning to exercise after breast augmentation recovery

At the two-week mark, patients can begin walking at a faster pace and incorporate light exercise into their routines.

sources.publisher: ASPS website, blog by John Q. Cook, MD
sources.title: Will breast implants get in the way of exercise?
quotes: Avoid chest and shoulder exercises, lifting weights or any other exercise that puts pressure on your chest or back.

The good news is that there will be no need to give up running, lifting weights or other forms of exercise after augmentation.
Implants should not prevent you from having an active lifestyle.
Always wear a supportive bra if you're exercising after breast augmentation

sources.title: What should I expect during my breast augmentation recovery?

sources.title: Breast Augmentation

On average, full recovery takes about six to eight weeks.

quotes: Symptoms of this include chest pain, shortness of breath, cough with blood, lightheadedness and fainting.

Also contact your surgeon if you notice sudden swelling of your breast.

sources.title: Breast Augmentation: What to expect and how to prepare (handout PDF)
quotes: Do not lift, pull, or push heavy objects for 2 weeks after your surgery.
